<!--
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. GitHub fills a pull request's title and description from
the commit ONLY when the branch has exactly one commit. With two or more it
gives up, titles the PR after the branch ("Dev"), and leaves the description
empty - so the PRs carrying the most work end up with the least explanation,
which is exactly backwards. Six months from now the PR list is what somebody
searches, and "Dev" tells them nothing.

Delete any heading that does not apply. A short honest PR beats a padded one.
-->

## What changed

<!-- One or two sentences. What is different for somebody using this, not which
     files moved. -->

## Why

<!-- The problem this solves. If it fixes something that was broken, say what
     was broken and how it showed up - that is the part worth finding later. -->

## Decisions worth arguing about

<!-- Anything a reviewer might reasonably have done differently, and why it went
     this way. Also what was deliberately NOT done. Skip if there is nothing. -->

## How it was verified

<!-- What was actually run, not what is believed to be true. "Planned against a
     real Postgres, rendered headless and looked at, npm test 142/142" - not
     "tested". If something could not be verified here, say so. -->

## Anything that needs a human

<!-- Migrations to apply, secrets to add, env vars to set, a command to run
     once. Leave blank if nothing. -->
